# build { #labdata.remote.build }

```python
labdata.remote.build(cfg, client=None, progress=False)
```

Catalog every repository the settings name on GitHub.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**cfg**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Config](`labdata.config.Config`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Settings supplying `owners` and `repos`.

<code>[**client**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[Client](`labdata.github.Client`)\]]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Client to read with. Defaults to a new one, authenticated as [](`labdata.github.token`) finds.

<code>[**progress**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [False]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Show a progress bar, one step per repository. Reading a whole organisation is otherwise silent for as long as it takes.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[List](`typing.List`)\[[Entry](`labdata.model.Entry`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Entries from every repository that publishes something. A repository that cannot be read is skipped with a [](`labdata.config.SourceWarning`) rather than failing the scan, as is an owner GitHub will not list and a repository named in the settings that is not there.
